summary: S. 4489, titled the Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authorization Act, authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to carry out the Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authority System project in Montana and North Dakota. The bill provides Federal assistance for planning, design, and construction, establishes cost-sharing requirements, makes power available from the Pick-Sloan Program for system operations, and authorizes appropriations totaling $602,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2037.

affected_groups.effect: Receive a safe and adequate municipal, rural, and industrial water supply through the authorized Water System.
affected_groups.group: Citizens of Dawson, Garfield, McCone, Prairie, and Richland Counties in Montana, and McKenzie County in North Dakota

affected_groups.effect: Enters into a cooperative agreement for Federal assistance, holds title to the Water System, and is responsible for paying power charges and non-Federal delivery costs.

key_provisions: Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to carry out the Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authority System project substantially in accordance with an October 2025 Bureau of Reclamation feasibility study.
Requires the Secretary to enter into a cooperative agreement with the Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authority to provide Federal assistance for planning, design, and construction.
Sets the Federal share of planning, design, and construction costs at a maximum of 75 percent (or a lesser amount determined by the Secretary), which is nonreturnable and nonreimbursable.
Permits the use of Federal funds for water intake, pumping, treatment, storage facilities, transmission pipelines, electrical power facilities, and certain existing public water system facilities.
Directs the Administrator of the Western Area Power Administration to make power available at the firm power rate to meet the operational requirements of the Water System.
Authorizes the appropriation of $602,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2037, subject to indexing for ordinary cost fluctuations and adjustments for unforeseen market volatility.
missing_information: The total overall cost of the Water System beyond the federal share is not explicitly stated in the text outside of the maximum federal funding authorization and percentage limits.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 4489, titled the Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authorization Act, authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to carry out the Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authority System project in Montana and North Dakota. The bill provides Federal assistance for planning, design, and construction, establishes cost-sharing requirements, makes power available from the Pick-Sloan Program for system operations, and authorizes appropriations totaling $602,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2037.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a federal partnership to construct a regional water system for parts of Montana and North Dakota, authorizing $602,000,000 in federal appropriations and providing dedicated electrical power access from the Pick-Sloan Program.
